mainTopic: The חזקה that houses are checked on the fourteenth, renting an unchecked house, and the Torah source for the חמץ deadline on ערב פסח.
overview: Earlier, the גמרא asked whether a house on the fourteenth of ניסן is presumed already checked for חמץ. It first tries to prove this from the ברייתא that believes everyone, even women, slaves and minors, about removing חמץ. The proof says everyone counts as a חבר for בדיקת חמץ, just as a חבר's produce is presumed tithed. After several rounds of back-and-forth about the ברייתא's wording, the גמרא shows the ברייתא can still fit the view that houses are presumed checked. It explains that the ברייתא speaks of a house known to be unchecked. There these people are believed, because בדיקת חמץ is only rabbinic; by Torah law ביטול is enough. Next, an איבעיא asks whether renting out a house as 'checked' that turns out unchecked is a מקח טעות. אביי's statement shows it is not, since people are glad to do a מצוה themselves or with their own money. Finally, the גמרא quotes the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about when to stop eating חמץ and asks for the Torah source that חמץ is forbidden from the sixth hour. אביי compares two verses to include the fourteenth, the גמרא challenges that reading, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The proof: the house is believed because it is presumed checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the ברייתא 'everyone is believed, even women, slaves and minors' must rest on a חזקה that houses are checked, because everyone counts as a חבר regarding בדיקת חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it because the house is presumed to be checked? This תנא holds that everyone is considered a חבר when it comes to checking for חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to answer the open question (is a house presumed checked on the 14th?) using the ברייתא that believes even נשים, עבדים, and קטנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are normally not valid witnesses. So why trust them here? The proof says their word is not the real reason. The real reason is that every Jew is like a חבר about בדיקת חמץ, so the house is already presumed checked (חזקתו בדוק).

keyTerms.meaning: Its presumed status is that it has been checked
People trusted to be careful with מצוות such as tithing and purity

steps.confusionAlert: Here a 'חבר' does not mean a friend. It is a technical term for someone known to be careful and trustworthy in observance.

phrases.english: Is it not because its presumptive status is 'checked',
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks this as a question, but it's really bringing a proof.

phrases.english: for he holds: all are considered ḥaverim
with regard to the search for leaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt to resolve the question of whether a house on the 14th is presumed checked, using the ברייתא of הכל נאמנים.
steps.raayaObject: That a house on the 14th has the status of חזקתו בדוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that believes even women, slaves and minors about ביעור חמץ

steps.title: Supporting source: a חבר who died leaving produce
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that a חבר is presumed to have done what he is obligated to do: his produce is presumed tithed, even if it was brought in that very day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a חבר who died and left a storehouse full of produce, even if the produce came in that same day, it is presumed to be properly tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel case to back up the idea that a חבר is presumed to have done his duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not worry that the חבר died before he could tithe. We assume he did it. In the same way, if everyone counts as a חבר for בדיקת חמץ, every house is assumed to have been checked.

keyTerms.meaning: Of that very day (brought in only today)

phrases.english: As it was taught: a ḥaver who died
and left a storehouse full of produce,
even if they are only from that day,
they are presumed to be tithed.
phrases.notes: We assume the חבר tithed them

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: חָבֵר שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ מְגוּרָה מְלֵיאָה פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim that a חבר is presumed to have done what he must do.
steps.raayaObject: That a חבר is presumed to fulfill his obligations
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the חבר who died and left a storehouse of produce

steps.title: Maybe their statement is the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps houses are not presumed checked, and the ברייתא relies on the fact that these people actually said they checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know? Perhaps it is different here, because these people (women, slaves, minors) said that they checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof and offers a different reason for the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the ruling comes from a חזקה. The rejection says the ruling may come from the actual statement of the woman, slave or minor. If so, the ברייתא says nothing about a house where nobody said anything.

phrases.english: And from where? Perhaps it is different here,
because these people said so.
phrases.notes: Women, slaves, or minors who stated that they checked

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 1-2 by suggesting another reason for the ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that the ברייתא depends on חזקתו בדוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling could depend on the explicit statement of these people, not on a general חזקה

steps.title: Their statement has no legal weight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the rejection. The word of women, slaves and minors carries no legal weight, so it cannot be the reason. The reason must be the חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the statement of these people have any substance? (They are not believed as witnesses!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the rejection from step 3, which brings the original proof back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are disqualified as witnesses, so their statement alone should prove nothing. That brings us back to the idea that the house must be presumed checked.

phrases.english: Is that to say that the statement of these people
has any substance to it?
phrases.notes: The expected answer is no, there's nothing to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ אֲמִירָה דְּהָנֵי מִידֵּי מְשָׁשָׁא אִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 3 and so restores the proof of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the statement of these people is the reason
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: These people are not credible witnesses, so their statement cannot be the legal basis

steps.title: If it is a חזקה, the ברייתא's wording does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חזקה reading. If the real reason were a חזקה, the ברייתא should have said 'all houses are presumed checked on the 14th,' not 'everyone is believed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, then: is it because the house is presumed checked? If so, instead of 'everyone is believed,' it should have said 'all houses are presumed checked on the fourteenth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the restored proof by pointing to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'everyone is believed' (הכל נאמנים) is about trusting a person's word. A rule based on a חזקה would talk about the houses themselves. So the wording suggests the people's statement does matter.

phrases.english: Rather, what? That its presumptive status is 'checked'?
Then instead of this 'everyone is believed',
'all houses are presumed checked
on the fourteenth' is what it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי — דְּחָזְקָתוֹ בָּדוּק? הַאי הַכֹּל נֶאֱמָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חזקה reading that step 4 restored, based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is based on חזקתו בדוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule based on a חזקה would be phrased about the houses, not about which people are believed

steps.title: If it is their statement, the question is answered the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters. If the ruling depends on the people's statement, then without a statement the house is not presumed checked. That would answer the original question: there is no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, then: is it because these people said so, and if they did not say so, no? Then resolve the question from here: the house is not presumed checked!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the other reading also leads to a strong conclusion, the opposite one: no חזקה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people's statement is what matters, the ברייתא implies that silence gives no assumption of checking. That would decide the question as אין חזקתו בדוק. The גמרא raises this as a counter-challenge, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: But if they did not say

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the ברייתא seem to have a problem. 'Everyone is believed' sounds like the people's word matters. But their word has no legal weight, and relying on it would mean there is no חזקה. The next step answers this by showing the חזקה can still stand, limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: each side of a dilemma is tested against the wording and logic of a source. The way the גמרא settles it will shape how we treat rented homes on ערב פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, what? Because of the statement of these people,
so if these people do not say so, then no?
Then resolve from it that its presumptive status is not 'checked'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 5: the statement-based reading that step 5 implies would itself decide the question against a חזקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא depends on the statement of these people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the statement is what matters, then without it there is no חזקה, which resolves the question as אין חזקתו בדוק

steps.title: Houses are presumed checked; the ברייתא is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the חזקה that houses are checked on the 14th. It explains that the ברייתא deals with a case where we know the owner did not check, and these people say they checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really I can tell you the house is presumed checked. What case is the ברייתא talking about? A case where we know he did not check, and these people say: 'We checked it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6. It keeps the חזקה and moves the ברייתא to an unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that if the ruling depends on the people's statement, there must be no חזקה. The answer is that the ברייתא is not talking about a normal house. It is talking about a house we know was not checked, so the חזקה is gone and only their statement is left. In a normal house the חזקה still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: I keep my original position
What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that limits a source to a specific case)
It is established to us / we know for sure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חזקה has been disproved. The גמרא shows that the ברייתא can still fit the view that houses are presumed checked, because it speaks of a special case where we know the owner did not check. This only deflects the proof. It does not prove the חזקה.

phrases.english: No, really I can say to you
its presumptive status is 'checked,'
and here, with what case are we dealing?
where it is established to us that he did not check,
and these people say: 'We checked it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ חֶזְקָתוֹ בָּדוּק, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counter-challenge of Step 6 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the ברייתא speaks of a house known to be unchecked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ברייתא relies on the people's statement, houses must not be presumed checked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא does not disprove the חזקה. One can still hold that houses are presumed checked, and the people's statement matters only where we know the owner did not check.

steps.title: Why they are believed: checking is only a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that women, slaves and minors are believed, because בדיקת חמץ is rabbinic. By Torah law ביטול alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the רבנן would not believe them. So the ברייתא teaches us: since checking for חמץ is only rabbinic, because by Torah law simple ביטול is enough, the רבנן believed them in a rabbinic matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point the ברייתא is teaching in this special case. People who normally cannot testify are believed here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women, slaves and minors are usually not trusted as witnesses, so we might think their word is worthless here too. But the Torah only requires ביטול, nullifying your חמץ in your mind. The search is a rabbinic addition, and the רבנן allowed these people to be trusted for their own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / lest you think
Nullifying your חמץ, declaring it ownerless like dust

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not disprove the view that houses are presumed checked on the 14th. Women, slaves and minors are believed about checking because בדיקת חמץ is rabbinic; by Torah law ביטול is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the principle that בדיקת חמץ is a rabbinic rule, and that the רבנן are more lenient about who is believed in their own rules.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the Rabbis should not believe them,
so it teaches us:
since checking for chametz is by rabbinic law,
for by Torah law mere nullification is enough for him,
the Rabbis believed them in a rabbinic matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לָא לְהֵימְנִינְהוּ רַבָּנַן, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of Step 7 by explaining what the ברייתא is teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא fits the view that houses are presumed checked on the 14th. Where it is known that the owner did not check, women, slaves and minors are believed because בדיקת חמץ is rabbinic.

steps.title: Renting out a house as 'checked' that turns out unchecked
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא: if someone rents a house as already checked and it turns out unchecked, is it a מקח טעות?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: someone rents a house to his friend on the understanding that it is checked, and the renter finds it is not checked. What is the law? Is it a mistaken deal, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about renting out a house on the assumption that it was checked. Can a renter cancel the deal because the house was not checked?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The renter agreed on the assumption that the house was checked. Now he must do the work or pay for it himself. The question is whether this mistake is serious enough to cancel the deal as a מקח טעות.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open legal question)
On the assumption that it is checked
A mistaken transaction, which can be cancelled

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
one who rents out a house to his fellow
on the assumption that it is checked,
and he found that it is not checked, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי הָוֵי כְּמִקָּח טָעוּת, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Is it like a mistaken transaction, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הַמַּשְׂכִּיר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵירוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת בָּדוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether houses are presumed checked to a monetary question about a house rented as 'checked'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a rental made on the assumption that the house was checked can be cancelled as a מקח טעות when it turns out unchecked.

steps.title: אביי: people are happy to do the מצוה themselves
steps.stepSummary: אביי's statement shows that it is not a מקח טעות. People are glad to do the מצוה with their own body, and even with their own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for אביי said: You don't even need to say this in a place where people don't pay someone and they check themselves, because a person is happy to do a מצוה himself. Even in a place where people pay someone to check, a person is happy to do a מצוה with his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אביי's statement to answer the question. The deal is not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where people check by themselves, the renter loses nothing. He is glad to do the מצוה in person. Even where people hire someone to check, it is still not a מקח טעות, because a person is glad to spend his own money on a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not even necessary to say (this case is obvious)
It is pleasing to him / he is happy with it
With his own body, in person

steps.confusionAlert: Read the לא מיבעיא in order. The first case, where people check by themselves, is the easy one. The 'even' case, where people pay someone to check, is the bigger point. In both cases it is NOT a מקח טעות.
steps.whatToRemember: Renting out a house as 'checked' that turns out unchecked is not a מקח טעות, because people are happy to do a מצוה themselves or with their own money.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Abaye said:
It is not even necessary to say
in a place where they do not give a wage and they check themselves,
for a person is pleased
to fulfill a מצוה with his own body.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ בְּאַתְרָא דְּיָהֲבִי אַגְרָא וּבְדַקוּ —
phrases.english: Rather, even in a place where they give a wage and have someone check,
for a person is pleased
to fulfill a מצוה with his own money.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is not a מקח טעות, because a person is happy to do the מצוה of checking himself or to pay for it.

steps.title: משנה: when to stop eating and when to burn חמץ
steps.stepSummary: A משנה elsewhere: רבי מאיר lets you eat חמץ for five hours and burn it at the start of the sixth. רבי יהודה lets you eat for four hours, wait during the fifth, and burn at the start of the sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: רבי מאיר says, we eat all of the fifth hour and burn at the beginning of the sixth. רבי יהודה says, we eat all of the fourth hour, hold it in suspense during the fifth, and burn at the beginning of the sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה about the times on ערב פסח. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about the fifth hour. רבי מאיר allows eating then. רבי יהודה forbids eating, but you do not have to burn the חמץ yet. Both agree that burning happens at the start of the sixth hour.

keyTerms.meaning: We leave it in suspense: no eating yet, but no burning yet either

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אוֹכְלִין כָּל חָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: we eat through all of the fifth hour,
and we burn at the beginning of the sixth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אוֹכְלִין כָּל אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: we eat through all of the fourth hour,
and we leave it in suspense through all of the fifth,
and we burn at the beginning of the sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אוֹכְלִין כָּל חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the rental question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: eat until the end of the fifth hour, burn at the start of the sixth. רבי יהודה: eat until the end of the fourth hour, suspend during the fifth, burn at the start of the sixth.

steps.title: What is the source that חמץ is forbidden from the sixth hour?
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that חמץ is forbidden from the sixth hour on. The גמרא asks for the source of this.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that חמץ is forbidden from six hours and onward. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agree on. Then it asks for the Torah source, which the next steps will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions disagree only about the fifth hour: רבי מאיר permits eating then, and רבי יהודה does not. Both allow eating through the fourth hour, and both agree that from the sixth hour, about midday, חמץ is forbidden by Torah law. The גמרא wants to know where in the Torah this deadline comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: According to everyone, in any case,
chametz from six hours and onward is forbidden;
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהָא חָמֵץ מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה אָסוּר, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the point both sides of the משנה in Step 11 agree on and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the prohibition of חמץ from the sixth hour on the 14th of ניסן.

steps.title: אביי's two verses point to the fourteenth
steps.stepSummary: אביי sets two verses side by side. One forbids שאור for all seven days. The other says to remove שאור 'on the first day.' He concludes that 'the first day' means the fourteenth of ניסן, so the duty to destroy חמץ starts before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Two verses are written. One verse says: 'For seven days, leaven shall not be found in your houses.' Another verse says: 'But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses.' How do these fit together? The second verse comes to include the fourteenth of ניסן for removing חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 12: where do we learn that חמץ is forbidden on the fourteenth? אביי brings a source by comparing two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the first day' meant the first day of פסח (the fifteenth), there would be a problem. The other verse already says no חמץ may be found during all seven days, so removing it only once פסח has begun would be too late. So אביי reads 'the first day' as the day before פסח, the fourteenth, which makes it the day for getting rid of חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses are written. This signals that the גמרא will compare two פסוקים.
Leaven, the sourdough starter. Here it stands for חמץ in general.
You shall remove, or make cease to exist.
How can this be? A formula for resolving a contradiction.
To include, meaning the verse adds something new.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'ביום הראשון' sounds like it must mean the first day of פסח. אביי's whole point is that it cannot mean that here. It refers to the fourteenth, the day before פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation is the first step toward the Torah-level basis for the ערב פסח deadline that both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agreed on in Step 11. It shows that the duty to remove חמץ already applies on the fourteenth, before פסח begins.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Two verses are written.
It is written: 'Seven days, leaven'
shall not be found in your houses.'
And it is written: 'But on the first day'
you shall remove leaven from your houses.'
How can this be?
phrases.notes: The two verses seem to clash.

phrases.english: It comes to include the fourteenth for removal.
phrases.notes: 'The first day' is read as the fourteenth of ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the source question asked in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Comparing the two verses shows that 'the first day' refers to the fourteenth, which is the day for removing חמץ.

steps.title: Maybe the verse adds the night of the fifteenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי. Perhaps 'the first day' is the fifteenth after all, and the verse comes to add the night of the fifteenth. Otherwise one might think 'seven days' covers only daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that it comes to include the night of the fifteenth for removing חמץ. You might have thought: the verse says 'days,' so days yes, nights no. So the verse teaches us that even the nights are included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reading of the second verse, which would remove אביי's proof for the fourteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof works only if the second verse has nothing else to teach. The challenge gives it another job: since 'שבעת ימים' mentions only days, one might think חמץ is allowed at night. On this reading, 'ביום הראשון' would teach that the first night is also forbidden. If so, the verse says nothing about the fourteenth.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead. This introduces a competing interpretation.
The night of the fifteenth, the first night of פסח.
It would have entered your mind to say. This describes a mistaken first impression.
It teaches us. This names the new lesson the verse would be coming to teach.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לְבִיעוּר,
phrases.english: But say instead it comes to include the night of the fifteenth for removal.
For it would have entered your mind to say:
'Days' is written,
so during days, yes; during nights, no.
So the verse teaches us: even nights!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's reading by giving the verse a different purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that 'ביום הראשון' must refer to the fourteenth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could be needed to add the nights of פסח, which 'שבעת ימים' might seem to leave out. That would make it unavailable as a source for the fourteenth.

steps.title: That teaching was not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: there is no need for this verse to teach about the nights. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was not needed for him,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to defend אביי by saying the verse is not needed to teach about nights. This is a setup line, and the reason comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nights are already included from some other source, the second verse is free again. It can then be used for the fourteenth, which restores אביי's proof. The other source is given in the continuation of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not needed, meaning the law is already known from elsewhere.
That one, here pointing to the idea that nights are included.

phrases.english: That was not needed for him,
phrases.notes: The reason why continues on the next amud.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is not needed for that teaching, because the law is learned elsewhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is needed to include the nights of the fifteenth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nights do not need this verse, so it remains available as a source for the fourteenth (the details continue next).
